caption:
Lemon Loaf 🍋 🍞 // How a chemical engineer would make the World’s best lemon loaf. I tested this one 8 times and got an addicting, moist, and dense lemon loaf. I’ve optimized it for intense lemon flavor but has other flavors in the background making it way better than one you buy at the store.

Recipe
This recipe is for a 8x4 loaf. If your pan is 9x5, multiply all ingredient measurements by 1.5. 

Loaf 
165g granulated sugar
Zest of 1 lemon
Zest of 1 lime
Zest of 1 orange 
1 tsp grated fresh ginger
1 egg
75g olive oil
65g almond milk
145g AP flour 
1 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
30g lemon juice (1/2 lemon)
10g lime juice (1/2 lime)

Lemon Syrup
30g lemon juice
15g lime juice 
25g Powdered sugar

1. This recipe is for a 8x4 loaf. If you are using a 9x5 loaf, multiply ingredient measurements by 1.5.
2. Preheat oven to 160C/320F convection/fan setting. Otherwise use 180C/350F if you do not have fan setting. Grease and line your loaf tin with parchment paper.
3. In a large bowl, add sugar, all zests, and fresh ginger. Rub all of these together with your fingers until the sugar is resembles yellow damp sand. Let sit for 15 minutes to absorb all the essential oils
4. Add egg and olive oil. Whisk and let sit 5 minutes. A lot the sugar should be dissolved after 5 minutes.
5. Add milk and whisk. Make sure all sugar is dissolved.
6. Add dry ingredients, lemon juice, and lime juice at the same time and mix until well combined.
7. Pour batter into lined loaf tin. Bake for 55-60 minutes the loaf will be golden should spring back when you press the top.
8. Prepare lemon syrup by mixing everything together. 
9. Once loaf is out, let rest for 10 minutes, then poke holes throughout the loaf with a skinny skewer. 
10. Spoon lemon syrup over the hot loaf. Make sure to get the edges. It’ll soak up the syrup quickly.

Optional: A glaze - mix runny Greek yogurt, powdered sugar, lemon juice until combined and drizzle over the top once nearly cooled
Pro tip: once cooled, wrap tightly in plastic wrap over night. It will be super moist the next day.
author: AYO FURY
transcript: This is how a chemical engineer makes the world's best lemon loaf. First, a chemical engineer would never bake at 180°C or 350°F. Citrus flavor comes from the flavor molecules limonene and citrile, which is thermally unstable. At 180°C, these are already beginning to degrade and evaporate off the loaf. That's why most loaves never really taste like lemon. So a chemical engineer would bake at 160°C to reduce some of the citrus degradation. Now lemon by itself can be a bit boring and even taste like soap. So to put it this way, you would never wear just a pure lemon cologne or perfume, right? It has to have like wood or floral notes in the background. Otherwise, it just smells like cleaning chemicals. The same concept applies to lemon loaf. In addition to limonene and citrile, lime contains pinyin and terpene, which are green wood and spice molecules found in pine trees, oregano, and thyme. Adding a little lime to your lemon syrup gives a background flavor to the lemon loaf and makes it far more satisfying to eat, but no one will know your secret. Wow. All because of science.
title: Chemical Engineer's Science-Backed Lemon Loaf
one_liner: A chemical engineer optimizes lemon loaf for intense citrus flavor using food science principles.
key_points: Bake at 160°C instead of 180°C to prevent limonene and citral (citrus flavor molecules) from degrading
Add lime zest and juice alongside lemon — lime's pinene and terpene molecules add woody/spice background notes that make the flavor more complex
Rub sugar with zests and ginger for 15 minutes to extract essential oils before mixing the batter
Poke holes and soak the hot loaf with lemon-lime syrup immediately after baking for maximum moisture

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C/320°F (convection) or 180°C/350°F (no fan). Grease and line an 8x4 loaf tin with parchment paper.
Combine sugar, all zests, and fresh ginger in a large bowl. Rub together with fingers until sugar resembles damp yellow sand. Let sit 15 minutes.
Add egg and olive oil; whisk and let sit 5 minutes until most sugar is dissolved.
Add milk and whisk until all sugar is dissolved.
Add flour, baking powder, salt, lemon juice, and lime juice all at once; mix until well combined.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Bake 55–60 minutes until golden and top springs back when pressed.
Mix syrup ingredients together. Let loaf rest 10 minutes out of oven, then poke holes throughout with a skewer.
Spoon lemon-lime syrup over hot loaf, covering edges. Allow to soak in.
Optional: drizzle a glaze of runny Greek yogurt, powdered sugar, and lemon juice once nearly cooled. Wrap cooled loaf tightly in plastic wrap overnight for maximum moisture.
